title: Phantom Blade Zero Collectibles - All Seven Types and What Each Gives
description: The world hides seven categories of collectibles, including three fragment types that permanently raise Soul's Sha-chi bar, attack and health. Bells double as fast travel and resource restock points. Bilingual names included.

sections.title: The seven categories
sections.content:
The world is built to be walked back through, and the collectibles are what mark whether you have actually explored it. Community documentation lists seven categories, and the game tracks a total and a completion percentage per map, so you can see what you skipped.

  1. Bells (铃铛) - the backbone of the map system, described in its own section below.
  2. Weapons and Phantom Edges (武器与影之武装) - pickups scattered through the world, some of which need a specific Phantom Edge to reach at all.
  3. Accessories and flasks (饰品与药瓶) - the gear and healing items that round out a build.
  4. Challenge locations (挑战地点) - optional fight areas with rewards on completion.
  5. Sha-chi Amber shards (杀气琥珀碎片) - community-documented as raising the Sha-chi bar cap by 10%.
  6. Black Stone shards (黑石碎片) - community-documented as raising attack and guard-breaking by 10%.
  7. Memory Flowers (记忆之花) - community-documented as raising maximum health by 10%.

Separate from those are story collectibles - notes and letters (纸条、信件) that sit in the world and can be re-read from the inventory. They carry lore rather than power, which makes them the category completionists are most likely to miss on a first pass.

sections.title: Bells do three jobs
sections.content:
The official State of Play described bells as the fast-travel mechanism. Community documentation adds two things that matter more in practice:

  • Touching a bell for the first time clears the fog on the minimap around it, so a bell is a map-reveal as well as a waypoint.
  • Bells restore combat resources, which makes them the rest point in a game where, by the same accounts, defeated enemies do not simply repopulate when you rest.
  • Travel runs between discovered bells, and a consumable teleport item (穿行符) lets you jump from anywhere back to one.

The practical consequence: bells are not just convenience, they are the economy of the map. If you are stuck on a boss, the answer is more often a bell you have not reached than a level you have not earned.

sections.title: The three permanent upgrades
sections.content:
Three of the seven categories are progression rather than loot, each reported by the community wiki as a flat 10% per pickup: Sha-chi Amber to the resource bar cap, Black Stone to attack and guard-breaking, Memory Flower to health. That is the closest thing this game has to a stat system, and it is exploration-driven rather than combat-driven - which is the design statement.

Marked as community-sourced. The exact percentage, whether it compounds linearly, and how many of each exist have not been published by S-GAME. Verify against the retail game before planning a route around them.

sections.title: Why you will come back
sections.content:
The October 2026 studio previews described Phantom Edges being used outside combat: an axe that smashes environmental barriers, a chain sickle that works as a grappling hook. That means some pickups in the seven categories are physically unreachable until you have the right secondary weapon, which is also why the per-map completion percentage exists at all - see missable content.

Treat any 80%-complete map as a promise rather than a mistake - the missing 20% is probably gated, and the game tells you how much you have left.
